item: Skill Runner for Local LLM Harness
best_architecture: Adopt Anthropic's now-open SKILL.md standard (folder per skill, each containing a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter + markdown body) and implement a three-tier progressive-disclosure loader, which is the single most important design decision. (1) DISCOVERY: at startup, glob-scan a layered set of skill roots in precedence order -- ~/.claude/skills/ (user/global), <project>/.claude/skills/ (project), and parent directories up to the repo root, plus nested monorepo dirs discovered on demand; match `**/SKILL.md`. (2) METADATA-ONLY INDEX: parse ONLY the YAML frontmatter (name, description, and optional trigger/tools/license/model fields) for every skill -- roughly 30-100 tokens each -- and build an in-memory registry. Inject only this lightweight catalog (name + description) into the system prompt so the model knows each skill exists and when to use it without paying the full-body context cost (e.g. 8 skills ~ 500 tokens vs ~70k if eagerly loaded). (3) LAZY ACTIVATION: only when a skill is selected (by the model emitting a tool/function call such as `load_skill(name)`, or by a deterministic trigger/keyword/regex match, or by an embedding-based retriever for large skill sets) do you read the full SKILL.md body from disk and append it to context; bundled resources under scripts/, references/, assets/ load on demand only when the body references them. Key design decisions: (a) Treat skill loading itself as a TOOL the Gemma model can call (a meta-tool / 'Search-and-Load' pattern) -- this scales far better than stuffing all skills into the prompt and aligns with RAG-for-tools research showing context-enriched retrieval improves accuracy ~50%. (b) Use a Pydantic schema to validate frontmatter at load time so malformed skills fail fast. (c) Maintain a loaded-skills set keyed by skill name for DEDUPLICATION, so a chained skill that invokes another already-loaded skill does not re-inject its body. (d) Skill CHAINING: let an activated skill's body reference other skills by name; the runner resolves the reference, checks the dedup set, lazy-loads if absent, and guards against cycles with a visited-set + max-depth. (e) Keep individual SKILL.md bodies under ~500 lines and push detail into reference files to preserve progressive disclosure. (f) For Gemma 4 specifically, surface the load_skill / invoke_tool functions through `apply_chat_template(..., tools=...)` (JSON-schema or Python-function tool defs) and parse the structured function-call output via the documented 4-stage Define->Model->Developer->Final loop; route everything through an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (llama.cpp / llama-server / Unsloth Studio / vLLM) so the harness stays model-agnostic. This mirrors Semantic Kernel's kernel+plugins model and LangChain's toolkit model, but the SKILL.md-on-filesystem + progressive disclosure approach is the most token-efficient and is directly portable from Claude Code.
reference_papers: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al. 2022) - arxiv:2210.03629 - Thought-Action-Observation loop; foundational paradigm for a skill/tool runner that interleaves reasoning with skill invocation

Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools (Schick et al. 2023) - arxiv:2302.04761 - self-supervised learning of when/how to call tools; rationale for letting the model decide skill activation

Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs (Patil et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.15334 - retrieval of relevant function/tool specs at inference time over 1,600+ APIs; directly motivates retrieval-based skill discovery instead of eager loading

Dynamic ReAct: Scalable Tool Selection for Large-Scale MCP Environments (2025) - arxiv:2509.20386 - 'Search and Load' meta-tool + vector retrieval architecture scaling to thousands of tools; context-enriched embeddings improve retrieval accuracy ~50% (maps directly to load_skill meta-tool design)

MemTool: Optimizing Short-Term Memory Management for Dynamic Tool Calling in LLM Agent Multi-Turn Conversations (2025) - arxiv:2507.21428 - managing which tools/skills stay loaded across turns; RAG over external tool stores; relevant to skill dedup and unloading

Dynamic Tool Dependency Retrieval for Efficient Function Calling (2025) - arxiv:2512.17052 - retrieval conditioned on both query and prior invoked tools; informs skill-chaining / dependency-aware activation [uncertain: exact arxiv id 2512.17052]
Tool-to-Agent Retrieval: Bridging Tools and Agents for Scalable LLM Multi-Agent Systems (Lumer et al. 2025) - arxiv:2511.01854 - retrieval bridging granular tools and higher-level agents/skills

Graph-of-Skills: Dependency-Aware Structural Retrieval for Massive Agent Skills (2026) - arxiv:2604.05333 - graph-structured retrieval over skill dependencies at scale; directly relevant to skill chaining/dedup [uncertain: pre-cutoff arxiv id 2604.05333]
reference_repos: anthropics/skills - Official public repository for Agent Skills; canonical SKILL.md folder format (frontmatter + scripts/ references/ assets/) and example skills - https://github.com/anthropics/skills

obra/superpowers-skills - Community-editable skills for Claude Code's superpowers plugin; cloned to ~/.config/superpowers/skills/; reference for skill layout, TDD/debugging skills and chaining patterns - https://github.com/obra/superpowers-skills

Hacker0x01/claude-power-user - Claude Code superpowers core skills library; SessionStart hook loads using-superpowers at startup, automatic discovery + mandatory-workflow activation; good reference for discovery/activation mechanics - https://github.com/Hacker0x01/claude-power-user

numman-ali/openskills - Universal SKILL.md loader for any AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, Codex); exact Claude Code format compatibility, progressive disclosure, installs from local paths or private git - https://github.com/numman-ali/openskills

instavm/open-skills - Run Claude Skills locally with ANY LLM via an MCP server in a sandboxed environment; closest direct analog to a local skill runner (SKILL.md + scripts/ + requirements.txt) - https://github.com/instavm/open-skills

openharness-ai (PyPI: openharness-ai) - Open-source Python agent harness; compatible with anthropics/skills (drop .md into ~/.openharness/skills/) and Claude Code plugins; reference implementation of harness + skill loading in Python - https://pypi.org/project/openharness-ai/

travisvn/awesome-claude-skills - Curated index of Claude skills, loaders and tooling (openskills, SkillsMP, etc.); good map of the ecosystem and progressive-disclosure conventions - https://github.com/travisvn/awesome-claude-skills

alirezarezvani/claude-skills - Large multi-agent skill library (330+ skills) with stdlib-only Python tools and a scripts/convert.sh to retarget skills to other agents; reference for portable, dependency-free skill scripts - https://github.com/alirezarezvani/claude-skills

microsoft/semantic-kernel - Kernel + plugins (semantic & native functions) architecture; reference for a structured, kernel-managed skill/plugin registry pattern - https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel [uncertain: exact repo path]
langchain-ai/langchain - Tools/Toolkits/Agents abstraction; reference for tool registration and agent-driven tool selection in Python - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain
key_libraries: python-frontmatter - Python - latest (1.x) - parse SKILL.md files splitting YAML frontmatter (name, description, trigger, tools) from the markdown body; primary frontmatter loader (frontmatter.load/loads)
PyYAML - Python - 6.x - underlying YAML parser for frontmatter and skill metadata; use yaml.safe_load when parsing untrusted frontmatter
ruamel.yaml - Python - latest - YAML 1.2-compliant alternative used by frontmatter-format; preferred when round-tripping/comment-preserving frontmatter is needed

pydantic - Python - 2.x - define and validate the skill frontmatter schema (name, description, trigger, tools, model, license) at load time; fail-fast on malformed skills and produce typed registry objects
pathlib / glob (stdlib) - Python - 3.11+ - filesystem discovery: recursive glob('**/SKILL.md') across ~/.claude/skills/, project .claude/skills/, parent dirs and nested monorepo dirs

transformers - Python - latest - Gemma 4 chat/tool integration via processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools, add_generation_prompt=True); standard system/user/assistant roles + native function calling
unsloth - Python - latest - fast local loading/fine-tuning/inference of Gemma 4 (and FunctionGemma) with built-in tool-calling setup; serve via Unsloth Studio / llama.cpp
llama-cpp-python (or llama.cpp llama-server) - Python/C++ - latest - run Gemma 4 GGUF locally behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so the skill runner stays model-agnostic

openai (python client) - Python - 1.x - talk to the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server/Unsloth/vLLM) for chat + tool-calling, decoupling harness from the specific backend [uncertain: whether project standardizes on openai client vs raw transformers]
frontmatter-format - Python - latest - LLM/agent-oriented frontmatter library (ruamel.yaml based, Pydantic-friendly) if richer metadata handling beyond python-frontmatter is desired
watchdog - Python - latest - optional filesystem watcher to hot-reload the skill registry when SKILL.md files change during development [uncertain: optional, only if hot-reload is a requirement]
